Example 3.13 asks for a molecular formula derived from percent composition (74.02% C, 8.710% H, 17.27% N) plus a molar mass obtained from 40.57 g / 0.2500 mol. Its worked chain is: percent composition -> empirical formula (C5H7N) -> empirical formula mass (81.13 amu) -> molar mass -> whole-number multiplier -> molecular formula. That is an empirical/molecular formula determination, which rule 4 lists explicitly as unregistered, so it is set aside rather than bent into a registered type.

Two near-fits were considered and rejected. (a) chemistry.molar-conversion: the passage does contain the pair 40.57 g and 0.2500 mol, but it uses them in the opposite direction — dividing mass by amount to obtain a molar mass — and the registered type computes an amount in moles from a stated mass and molar mass. No molar mass is given; it is the intermediate result. Formalising it would require taking a quantity from the answer side, which rule 1 forbids. (b) chemistry.mass-balance: no chemical equation appears at all.

The Check Your Learning answer C8H10N4O2 belongs to a different compound and a different question, and per rule 2 is not carried as the worked example's asserted result. So even under a hypothetical registered formula type there would be no readable result for the example's own givens; the primary and sufficient reason remains no_registered_problem_type.
